subject: After-action technical synopsis and validation plan
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Alice Park <alice.park@clearwave.com>, ops@clearwave.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 12 Jan 2027 09:02:00 -0800
Subject: After-action technical synopsis and validation plan

Hi Alice / ClearWave ops team,

Thank you again for the time on the call this morning. As promised, attached is our concise after-action technical synopsis of the service disruption on 2027-01-08, plus a proposed validation plan that we will execute with your team before we close the ticket. The packet includes: 1) a plain-language timeline, 2) the technical root cause summary, and 3) a verification playbook with acceptance criteria.

Key summary (short):
- What happened: A rare mismatch in KV-cache shard assignment combined with an autoscaler race resulted in transient tokenization regressions for a subset of ClearWave inference requests between 07:18 and 07:42 PST.
- Impact: ~0.8% of requests received degraded tokenization; median latency remained within SLO but some tail errors surfaced.
- Immediate fix: We reverted the autoscaler change and applied a guard to shard affinity logic; KV-cache eviction now uses a deterministic fallback.

Requested next steps from ClearWave: confirm the verification window you prefer (we propose a 48-hour staged verification starting 2027-01-14), and confirm whether you'd like us to run an isolated replay with your synthetic prompt set before any production ramp.

Attachments: clearwave_after-action_synopsis.pdf (concise RCA), verification-playbook.md (step-by-step checks), evidence-timeline.csv

I'll loop in Marissa and Grace for operational owners and timelines below. Happy to jump on a quick sync to walk the packet through.

Thanks,
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com
Redwood Inference

From: Alice Park <alice.park@clearwave.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@clearwave.com
Date: Wed, 13 Jan 2027 10:44:00 -0800
Subject: Re: After-action technical synopsis and validation plan

Vivek — thanks for the packet and for the clear summary. Quick acknowledgements: we appreciate the concise timeline and the deterministic fallback change looks promising. A few clarifying questions before we confirm the verification window:

1) Can you confirm whether any customer data was part of the affected KV-cache entries (we need a simple yes/no and a supporting statement about retention/erasure)?
2) In the verification playbook, the step that replays synthetic prompts references a ‘masked-token baseline’. Can you share the exact baseline file you plan to use so our privacy team can review?
3) If we proceed with the 48-hour staged verification, what is the rollback plan and the expected client-visible window if issues reappear?

We'd like a brief response to those points and a Doc link for the baseline file. Assuming those look good we are prepared to do the staged verification starting 2027-01-14 as you proposed.

—Alice
Director, Platform Ops
ClearWave

On Tue, Jan 12, 2027 at 09:02, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com> wrote:
> Thank you again for the time on the call this morning. As promised, attached is our concise after-action technical synopsis...

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alice Park <alice.park@clearwave.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 14 Jan 2027 08:17:00 -0800
Subject: Re: After-action technical synopsis and validation plan

Hi Alice — thanks for the questions. Short answers here and then the playbook has the linked artifact for the baseline.

1) Customer data: No ClearWave customer payloads were written to persistent storage as a result of the event. The affected KV-cache entries were ephemeral model state and masked token indexes. We have attached a short evidence note in the Drive link showing cache occupancy and eviction policy during the window.

2) Baseline file: Link is here — https://drive.redwood.ai/shared/ClearWave/after-action-jan2027/baseline-mask-v2.json. This file contains only synthetic prompts and hashed token indices; no customer text. Our Privacy & Security team has reviewed it (summary in the packet).

3) Rollback plan: If verification detects regression above 0.2% error rate on your acceptance suite, we will immediately remove the new shard affinity guard and reapply the previous safe settings; expected client-visible window during rollback is <30 minutes while we drain active batches. We will also issue a status update via your preferred channel.

Operational owners and timeline (we commit to):
- Validation lead: Marissa Cole — will run the replay and aggregate results (target: 2027-01-14 08:00–20:00 PST).
- Engineering escalation: Grace O'Connor — will be on-call for any live mitigation (24-hour coverage during validation).
- Evidence & compliance: Vivek Kulkarni — will provide the audit bundle and attestations by 2027-01-15 EOD.

I’ve opened JIRA SUP-3249 to track verification artifacts and outcomes. We will share run logs (redacted) and a short acceptance report when the run completes.

Attachments: verification-playbook.md (step-by-step), evidence-timeline.csv

Thanks — Marissa
Senior Manager, Customer Reliability
marissa.cole@redwood.com
Redwood Inference

Marissa / Vivek — this looks good and thank you for the speed. We reviewed the baseline file and the privacy summary; the answers are satisfactory. ClearWave confirms the staged verification window for 2027-01-14 and will standby for the acceptance report. If the error rate stays below 0.2% on our suite and the audit bundle is complete we will sign off on closure.

Next: please send the SUP-3249 verification report link and a short executive summary when available; ops@clearwave.com will expect the final acceptance by 2027-01-15 20:00 PST.

Appreciate the quick, transparent handling.

Best,
Alice Park
Director, Platform Ops
ClearWave
